In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

`in crystallo' substrate-binding triggers major domain movements in T. brucei PYK and reveals Mg(2+) as a co- activator of the enzyme, and that the interplay of side-chains with the bound metal ion explains the mechanism of the movement.
the T. brucei PYK is an allosteric enzyme that is activated by F26BP and that Mg(2+) is an obligate co-activator.
the T. brucei PYK-F26BP-Mg(2+)-PEP complex structure provides the first `in crystallo' view of how the substrate PEP binds to PYK and triggers a large domain movement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T. brucei PYK-F26BP-Mg(2+) structure represents the R-state of the enzyme, whereas the T. brueci PYK-F26P-Mg(2+)-PEP structure is a `closed' form of the R-state.
`in crystallo' PEP binding to PYK is a two-step process.
the enzyme from Try. brucei is a true `biphasic' allosteric protein with the two effectors F26BP and PEP each having a distinct role to play in the regulation of activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
`in crystallo' binding of PEP triggers major domain movements, and this may have important implications for the design of new antitrypanosomal agents.
`effector-only', `substrate-only', and `effector + substrate' structures are all necessary to understand the allosteric regulation of PYK.
